findings.reason: a node implementing this section finds its red arm green at base and either fudges the fixture or discovers the real defect is elsewhere, so the section must be rewritten around an actual reproduction before it is dispatched.
findings.text: §16's negative control cannot fail: its fixture is a live review pointer with empty `reviewed_run_id`/`review_subject` whose node id is the composed review node, and that shape is already suppressed at base — `_review_subject` falls through to `_resolved_reviewed_run_id` (recovery_review_dispatch.py:358) and `_review_head_covers("", head)` returns True (recovery_review_dispatch.py:373), so `_in_flight_review` returns the review run and `_current_review_in_flight` keeps the duty off; `review-missing` is assigned only when `superseded` (obligations.py:1008), which needs a stored record at a different head. The base arm would therefore not produce `review-missing`, and the "both fields empty" premise is also not the real pointer's shape — the cited review run's declared write paths name the reviewed run and its head (`…/review-records/r-20261024T045518148505-the-pane-shows-every-state-change.at-91b43f760035….json`), so the real recognition path was the record-path arm, not the node-id fallback.

findings.reason: a mechanism that does not reach the step that failed lets the section close green while the measured `review-missing` duty still appears, so the plan must bind the repair to the reproduced step rather than to a guess.
findings.text: §16 states the cause is not yet known ("name in the manifest which step failed to tie the review to its run (head, rubric, phase, or the snapshot the hook read). Fix that step") but its done-when fixes the outcome as node-id recognition plus recording the reviewed run's id on the pointer; neither touches the record-path arm the cited review actually carried, nor the snapshot the hook read — the two plausible failing steps the section itself lists.

findings.reason: the same node writes the row and the word, so it can settle the `to_state` in one place and the gate ("prints it once") catches a mismatch; naming it would tighten the brief but does not change what the node must build.
findings.text: §17 says `seat moved` "becomes a pane word of its own and a member of the carried words", but a pane word is selected by `_display_state` only when the row's `to_state` is a member of that word's frozenset in `PANE_STATES` (ticker.py:783-787), and the section never names the `to_state` the release row will carry, so the word and the row it is meant to match are specified independently.

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — the run §16 cites (`r-20261024T210847645911-review-of-the-pane-shows-every-state-change-91b43f760035`) and every symbol it names (`recovery_review_delivery._resolved_reviewed_run_id`, `recovery_review_dispatch._review_subject`) resolve.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §16's negative control cannot go red, because the fixture it describes is already recognised by the code the plan says is only a fallback.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the three units' gates record to their run's gate log, and §17 writes to the project's watch stream through `run_paths.watch_stream_path`, both durable.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the new pane words (`in review`, `seat moved`) are surface vocabulary, not plan labels, and no ticket numbers or version tags reach a symbol.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §16 says the failing step is unknown and must be reproduced, then fixes recognition through the one path that already works.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §15 (one suppression rule), §16 (one recognition defect) and §17 (one seat-release row) each name one deliverable with one gate.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — the three changed units' dependencies resolve: §17 names §15's ticker.py ordering, §16 is independent, and the open followup f-alwh-005 ("§15, §16 and §17, then §13, then the census") matches the write paths each section declares.
